newsitem.title: USA: More US steelmakers paying managers based on stock.
newsitem.headline: More US steelmakers paying managers based on stock.

text.p: U.S. steelmakers are increasingly linking executive pay to stock performance, signaling that an underperforming industry may be trying to reverse its reputation and be more shareholder friendly, industry officials and analysts say.
"This is an industry that has been underperforming to such an extent, it's mind boggling," said Chuck Bradford at UBS Securities.

Bradford said the industry has been underperforming largely because of weak pricing but then has been notorious for paying bonuses to senior executives from asset sale proceeds rather than recording proceeds as nonrecurring items.
"(Integrated steelmakers) need to tie management more to the shareholder," he said.

Shareholders of U.S. Steel Group, the nation's largest steelmaker, in '94 approved a compensation plan for senior officers that rewards them based on common stock performance, as well as factors including operating profit and shipments.
